Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

pattern noun

a regular way things happen

also a regular pattern, the same pattern, follow a pattern, sequence

classical

Cic. N. D. 2.97: tam ratōs astrōrum ōrdinēs
Cic. Off. 1.17: modum quendam et ōrdinem adhibentēs

ōrdō, ōrdinis m.

noun, third declension

a regular order, the way things follow one another

Lewis & Short: “right order, regular succession”; eundem ōrdinem tenēre, to keep to the same pattern (Cic. Phil. 5.35, Lewis & Short). For patterns of behaviour see practice (custom) and behaviour; for a pattern to copy, model; for a pattern on cloth, design.

Examples

  • Quis enim hunc hominem dīxerit, quī, cum tam certōs caelī mōtūs, tam ratōs astrōrum ōrdinēs … vīderit, neget in hīs ūllam inesse ratiōnem …?

    For who would call him a man who, seeing such regular movements in the sky and such fixed patterns in the stars, denies that there is any reason in them?Cic. N. D. 2.97

  • in ejus locum succēdit ex hīs, quae adquiērunt, eaque vicissitūdō in omnī cursū cōnservātur

    one of those that have rested takes the leader’s place, and this rotation is kept up the whole way (of cranes flying in a wedge)Cic. N. D. 2.125

Other words

  • vicissitūdō, vicissitūdinis f. — a regular alternation; taking turns

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. N. D. 2.125: eaque vicissitūdō in omnī cursū cōnservātur; Cic. Leg. 2.16: vicissitūdinēs diērum noctiumque (Lewis & Short)

    Of things that come round in turn: day and night, the seasons, people or birds taking turns.

See also order, practice, system, design, model, take turns.

SourcesLewis & Short: ordo · Lewis & Short: vicissitudo

Cicero, De natura deorum 2 and De officiis 1, checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (9 November 2026).
